children.text: The bell tower of Cagsawa Church, destroyed in Mayon Volcano's great

eruption, stands alone against the backdrop of a near-perfect volcanic cone. Carrying a tragic history, it's one of the Philippines' most iconic views, popular for early-morning photography and as the starting point for ATV tours across the lava fields.

The Cagsawa Ruins are the remains of the old Cagsawa Church, in the village of Busay in Daraga, Albay province. Franciscan friars built the church in the early 18th century, said to have been erected on this site around
. At the time, Cagsawa was one of the most prosperous towns in the Albay region.
On
February 1, 1814

, Mayon Volcano produced the most destructive eruption in its recorded history. Pyroclastic flows, ash, and hot rocks buried Cagsawa and the surrounding villages, and residents who took shelter in the sturdy stone church found even it engulfed by volcanic debris. This eruption is believed to have killed around 1,200 people. The town was later relocated elsewhere, leaving only the church's bell tower and part of its walls standing as ruins.
The church's history goes back further. The Franciscans first built a church at Cagsawa in
, and it is said to have been burned by Dutch pirates on
. The bell tower you see today dates from the
reconstruction. The death toll of the

eruption is generally given as around 1,200, though some sources put it at 2,000. The surviving residents moved to neighboring Daraga, and the two towns merged into one, which is today's municipality of Daraga. In
December 2015
the National Museum of the Philippines designated the ruins a National Cultural Treasure, the highest category of cultural property, and the site lies
11 km
from Mayon's summit. The National Museum Bicol branch inside the park was damaged by Typhoon Reming in
and operated from Tabaco City during
; after renovations it reopened next to the ruins in

Today, the Cagsawa Ruins are maintained as a park. The scorched-looking bell tower stands alone on a green lawn, with the perfectly conical Mayon Volcano rising behind it — one of the most frequently seen images in Philippine tourism promotion and postcards. Inside the park is a branch of the National Museum of the Philippines, introducing the
eruption and local history, and the surrounding area has souvenir shops, restaurants, and ATV tour operators.
The site is small, so visiting the ruins takes only about
1 hour

. But walking slowly while reflecting on the tragic history behind this beautiful scene leaves a deeper impression. It's recommended for history-minded travelers, those seeking the best photo of Mayon, and adventure travelers who want to ride an ATV across the volcano's base.

blocks.title: Frame the tower and Mayon together

children.text: The classic composition comes from the lawn near the park entrance, with the bell tower in front and Mayon behind. Shift slightly left or right so the tower and the summit don't overlap.
The summit of Mayon is often clouded over after
. Arriving right when the park opens in the early morning gives you a better chance of seeing the whole volcano, and there are fewer visitors too.
The small museum inside the park displays records from the
eruption, excavated artifacts, and the history and culture of the Albay region. It greatly deepens your understanding of what the ruins mean.
Around the bell tower, parts of the church's walls and foundation remain. Walk through the space where the plaza and church once stood and imagine the scale of the town at the time.
ATV tours depart from the starting point right next to the ruins. The meadow-and-forest routes are short, at around
30 minutes–1 hour
, while the Green Lava and Black Lava trails take
2–3 hours

. It is the experience that lets you feel Mayon from the closest range, but during the 2026 eruptive activity the routes inside the 6 km permanent danger zone were closed, so fewer routes are available. Confirm which routes are running before you book.
At the park entrance, shops line up selling bags and hats woven from abaca (Manila hemp) fiber, pili nut treats, and Mayon-shaped models.
About
10 minutes
away by car, Daraga Church is a Baroque church built from volcanic stone in
. Seen together with the Cagsawa bell tower, it gives a full picture of Albay's intertwined history of Spanish-era churches and volcanic eruptions.
From
February 1–28

, events commemorating the 1814 eruption are held centered on the ruins park. Local events such as an opening ceremony, a street dance competition, and a beauty pageant follow one another, so the park is busier than usual during this period. The schedule differs each year, so check announcements from the Daraga municipal government.

Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific fly from Manila to Bicol International Airport (DRP), about
1 hour
, with one-way fares of roughly
. The airport is in Daraga, about
30 minutes
by car from the Cagsawa Ruins.
Buses to Legazpi run daily from the Cubao, Pasay, and PITX terminals in Manila, taking about
12–13 hours
and costing about
. Many routes pass through Daraga, so you can also ask the driver to drop you at the Cagsawa entrance.
This route is currently run by DLTB, Raymond, and others. Philtranco, which ran the Bicol route for a long time, stopped operating from
March 30, 2026
Services differ a lot by operator. Bicol Isarog departs from PITX and Cubao, with regular air-conditioned seats at about
, Elite at about
, and sleeper at about
; the trip takes
9–14 hours
. DLTB has several departures a day from Cubao, with regular at about
and Lazy Boy at about
, taking around
12 hours 30 minutes
. Buses arrive at the Legazpi Grand Central Terminal (near Bitano and Landco Business Park), and premium seats sell out early, so book ahead.
From downtown Legazpi, take a Daraga-bound jeepney for about
20 minutes
, then transfer to a Cagsawa-bound jeepney or tricycle for another
10 minutes
. Jeepney fare is about
per leg, and tricycles run about
. For an early morning visit, chartering a tricycle from Legazpi is easier, at around
including the round trip and waiting time. You can also use a half-day tour run by a Legazpi hotel, or pickup service from an ATV operator.
From Cebu, Cebgo operates direct flights to Bicol International Airport (DRP), taking about
1 hour 15 minutes

. Cebgo also connects to Iloilo City. From most other cities you need to transfer in Manila, and no direct flight from Clark could be confirmed. Flight schedules change each season, so check the airline's app.
It is about
527 km

from Manila to Legazpi, heading south via the South Luzon Expressway (SLEX) and the STAR Tollway, then down the Maharlika Highway (Pan-Philippine Highway). Depending on traffic it takes more than 10 hours, so it is safer to stay overnight along the way or have a relief driver. From downtown Legazpi to the ruins is about
8 km
, usually
15–30 minutes
, and there is a parking lot in front of the ruins.

The train from Manila to Legazpi (the Bicol Express) is not running at present. The Bicol Commuter train on the Naga–Legazpi section also stopped after Super Typhoon Uwan damaged a bridge in Guinobatan in
November 2025
, and as of
July 2026
it is under repair and has not resumed. Check the Philippine National Railways (PNR) announcements for news of its resumption.
Clear weather to see Mayon is the key to this trip. The period with relatively less rain, from
February
to
May
, is best, with especially clear days in
March–April
. The Bicol region sees frequent rain year-round, so even in the dry season, afternoon showers and clouds are common.
From
June
to
December
is the rainy and typhoon season. Especially from
September–December
, strong typhoons often cross the Bicol region, disrupting flights and buses, and after heavy rain, lahar (volcanic mudflow) can occur on the volcano's slopes, sometimes suspending ATV tours.
During the day, Mayon is most visible from just after sunrise until
. If you're lucky, the clouds can also clear at sunset, giving you Mayon against a red sky.
Legazpi's average annual temperature is
. January, the coolest month, averages
, and May–June, the hottest, averages

. Annual rainfall is about 3,590 mm; even April, the driest month, gets about 152 mm, and December reaches about 642 mm. No month is completely dry, even in the dry season, so don't bank on a single date — build at least one extra day into your schedule and aim for a morning when Mayon is visible.
February 1
is the anniversary of the 1814 eruption, and the Cagsawa Festival runs for a month. During Super Typhoon Uwan in
November 2025
, lahar flowed down Mayon's slopes and a state of calamity was declared in Albay province; in typhoon season, roads and rivers around the ruins can be affected in this way.

items.label: Legazpi lodging
items.note: Per night, guesthouse to mid-range hotel

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
There isn't much lodging around the Cagsawa Ruins, so staying in downtown Legazpi, about
30 minutes
away by car, is standard. Legazpi has many mid-range hotels around
per night, including some with rooms that face Mayon. For a quieter option, small hotels or guesthouses in Daraga town are also fine.

Around the park entrance are small restaurants serving Bicolano home cooking. You can enjoy Bicol Express, seasoned with coconut milk and chili; laing, taro-leaf stew; and ginataan, a spicy fish dish simmered in coconut milk, all at reasonable prices. Back in Legazpi, a popular route is 1st Colonial Grill, an established restaurant known for Bicolano dishes and chili ice cream. For souvenirs, pili brittle (pili nuts set in sugar), pili tarts, and sweet pili candy make good choices.
The cheapest lodging in Legazpi starts at about
per night. If you want a view of Mayon, The Oriental Legazpi on Taysan Hill is a leading upscale hotel with Mayon-view rooms, while Hotel Venezia in the city center starts from about
per night. Prices at both vary greatly by date, so check on a booking site. If you're shooting at dawn, lodging on the Daraga side, close to the ruins, cuts your travel time.
If photography is your goal, arrive just after sunrise. It clouds over on many days after
, and group tours also crowd in.
Before visiting, check the current Mayon alert level from PHIVOLCS. At higher alert levels, ATV routes may be shortened or suspended.
Since there are several ATV operators, compare routes, duration, riders per vehicle, and safety gear. If you have no driving experience, you can choose a two-seater with a guide driving.
After an ATV tour, you'll be covered head to toe in volcanic ash dust. Bring disposable clothes, a change of clothes, a mask, and sunglasses.
The park entrance and surrounding shops mostly accept cash only. Bring plenty of small bills.
The lawn in front of the bell tower has little shade. Bring a hat, water, and sunscreen.
Souvenir prices vary by shop, so it's worth browsing a few and haggling a bit.
The park usually opens at
6–7 AM
and closes at
6 PM
(varies slightly by source). Admission is
for adults,
for seniors and persons with disabilities, and
for students and children, and parking is
for cars and
for motorcycles and tricycles.
The National Museum Bicol Branch right next to the ruins has no admission fee. Check the days and hours of operation on the
official National Museum page

Even during a Mayon alert, you can view Mayon from the safe viewing sites designated by the Albay tourism authority (PTCAO). The Cagsawa Ruins Park, Legazpi Boulevard, Sawangan Park, Daraga Church, and the National Museum are on that list. The designation of viewing sites changes with the alert level.
The bell tower is a heritage site over 200 years old. Climbing on it or touching and prying off bricks is prohibited.
When Mayon's alert level is high, the ruins park itself may be closed, or nearby areas may be placed under evacuation order. Follow local authority guidance.
After heavy rain, lahar can occur in nearby streams and gullies. Always follow your guide's instructions during ATV tours as well.
Helmets are mandatory on ATVs, and speeding or leaving the course can cause a rollover accident.
Confirm the fee up front with any freelance guides or photographers touting for business around the park.
In
Mayon was raised to Alert Level 3 in January and lowered to Level 2 in early
August

. It was still at Level 2 at the end of September, but alert levels change frequently. The permanent danger zone within a 6 km radius is off-limits, and the Green Lava and Black Lava trails, Mayon Skyline, and Mayon Natural Park inside it are closed. The ruins (about 11 km from Mayon's summit) lie outside the zone and are open. Before you leave, check announcements from PHIVOLCS and guidance from the Albay tourism authority.
Cagsawa is the site of a tragedy in which more than 1,000 people lost their lives. Please remember it as a place of remembrance before it is a photo spot.
The near-perfect volcanic cone rising behind the ruins, viewable from various angles at Ligñon Hill and Camalig, among other places.
